goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:72 — Unknown usernames are skipped while the endpoint still returns success, so a partial membership update can silently pass.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the add_members method in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb lines 62-77, the code iterates through usernames and only adds users that are found (if user = User.find_by_username(username)). If a username doesn't exist, it's silently skipped. The method then returns success_json if group.save succeeds, regardless of whether all usernames were valid. This means if an admin tries to add 'user1,user2,nonexistent_user', only user1 and user2 would be added, but the response would indicate success with no indication that 'nonexistent_user' was not found. This is a real correctness/UX issue where partial failures are not communicated to the caller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — The existing public group-members endpoint now returns an object instead of its prior serialized array, breaking clients that consume the response without a versioned compatibility path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the /groups/:group_id/members endpoint in groups_controller.rb changed from returning `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which returns an array) to returning `render json: { members: serialize_data(...), meta: {...} }` (which returns an object with 'members' and 'meta' keys). This is a breaking change to the API response format. The frontend templates were updated (group/members.hbs changed from `{{#each m in model}}` to `{{#each m in members}}`), but any external clients or other code consuming this public endpoint would break. This is a real backwards compatibility issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — The admin group create/update endpoints no longer accept the established nested `group` payload, so existing callers send fields that are silently ignored or fail.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the create method changed from expecting params[:group][:name] and params[:group][:usernames] to expecting params[:name] directly. The old code was `group.name = (params[:group][:name] || '').strip` and `group.usernames = params[:group][:usernames]`. The new code is `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip`. Similarly, update changed from `payload = params[:group]` to accessing params directly. However, looking at the JavaScript side, the create/save methods also changed - the old `createWithUsernames` sent `{group: {...}}` via `this.asJSON()` which returned `{group: {...}}`, but the new `create` method sends `this.asJSON()` which now returns just `{name:..., alias_level:..., visible:...}` without the `group` wrapper. So the frontend was updated to match the backend changes. The finding claims 'existing callers' would be broken, but the diff shows the callers (in the JS models) were also updated to use the new flat structure. This is a coordinated change, not a breaking change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The unbounded client-controlled `limit` can serialize an entire large group in one request.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb, line 22 shows `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`. The limit is taken directly from user input with only a default of 50 if not provided. There is no maximum cap on this value, so a client could pass limit=1000000 to retrieve and serialize all users in a group in one request. This is a real security/performance issue - unbounded pagination limits can lead to denial of service or excessive resource consumption.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Adding a large username list performs one user lookup per entry instead of a set-based lookup.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, line 71 in admin/groups_controller.rb shows the add_members method which iterates through usernames with `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and performs `User.find_by_username(username)` for each one. This is indeed an N+1 query pattern where each username requires a separate database lookup instead of using a single query like `User.where(username: usernames.split(","))`. This is a real performance issue - for a list of N usernames, it makes N database queries instead of 1.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The new paginated members response has no controller/request coverage for its JSON shape, ordering, or limit/offset boundaries.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points out that the new paginated members endpoint lacks test coverage for its JSON response shape, ordering, and pagination boundaries. Looking at the diff, the groups_controller.rb was modified to return a new JSON structure with members array and meta object containing total/limit/offset. The spec file changes shown are incomplete (cut off at line 'xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id:'). While there may be missing test coverage, this is a test coverage concern rather than a bug, security issue, or correctness problem in the actual code. The code itself appears functional - it queries users, applies limit/offset, and returns the expected JSON structure. Missing tests is a quality/process concern, not a defect in the code being reviewed.
